landmarks.name: Mount Everest
landmarks.writeup: The world's highest peak at 8,848 meters, located in the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border.

landmarks.name: Pashupatinath Temple
landmarks.writeup: A sacred Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, situated on the banks of the Bagmati River in Kathmandu.

landmarks.name: Boudhanath Stupa
landmarks.writeup: One of the largest spherical stupas in Nepal, a significant pilgrimage site for Buddhists.

landmarks.name: Chitwan National Park
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its wildlife, including Bengal tigers and one-horned rhinoceroses.

landmarks.name: Lumbini
landmarks.writeup: The birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama (Buddha), an important pilgrimage site for Buddhists worldwide.

cultural_events.name: Dashain
cultural_events.writeup: The longest and most significant Hindu festival in Nepal, celebrating the victory of good over evil.

cultural_events.name: Tihar
cultural_events.writeup: Also known as the Festival of Lights, it honors various animals and deities over five days.

cultural_events.name: Holi
cultural_events.writeup: The vibrant festival of colors marking the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil.

cultural_events.name: Teej
cultural_events.writeup: A fasting festival celebrated by women for marital happiness and the well-being of their spouses.

cultural_events.name: Indra Jatra
cultural_events.writeup: A festival in Kathmandu honoring the god Indra with masked dances and chariot processions.

food_writeup: Nepalese cuisine is diverse, featuring staples like dal bhat (lentil soup with rice), momo (dumplings), and gundruk (fermented leafy greens). It reflects a blend of Tibetan, Indian, and indigenous flavors.
brief_history: Nepal was unified in the 18th century by King Prithvi Narayan Shah. It remained a monarchy until 2008 when it became a federal democratic republic. The country has a rich history influenced by Hinduism and Buddhism and has maintained its sovereignty despite regional pressures.

important_people.name: Tenzing Norgay
important_people.description: Sherpa mountaineer, first to summit Everest with Edmund Hillary

important_people.name: Pushpa Kamal Dahal (Prachanda)
important_people.description: Former Prime Minister and Maoist leader

important_people.name: Siddhartha Gautama (Buddha)
important_people.description: Born in Lumbini, founder of Buddhism

current_conflicts: Nepal is generally peaceful but faces occasional political instability and challenges related to border issues with China and India. There are no active armed conflicts.
